column1: # Game profile of Balatro (Switch, update 1.1.3 = v851968). Plays on the iPhone; on the Mac through the title into a run (touch: the mouse), with sound
# LÖVE 11.4 ("Mysterious Mysteries", love-nx) with LuaJIT 2.1.0-beta3 in its interpreter, on SDL, SDK 18.3.2: the game itself is Lua source in the RomFS (main.lua, game.lua, engine/,
# functions/), its pictures PNG, its sound Ogg Vorbis. It renders with NVIDIA's desktop OpenGL 4.5 through EGL (subsdk0, not loaded): main gets its GL functions from LÖVE's glad
# loader (eglGetProcAddress) and calls about 150 of them (dm/tools/loader_census.py), which the host's GL layer implements on Metal (dm/gfx/gl/hle_gl.m), on the core profile's paths.
# main imports vkGetInstanceProcAddr only for SDL's Vulkan loader, which nothing uses (subsdk1 is NVIDIA's Vulkan driver, not loaded either)
# The shaders are GLSL that LÖVE puts together at run time, in Lua, from the game's 19 resources/shaders/*.fs files and its own built-in code: no game file holds them, so the NSP
# script captures them by booting the game on the Mac (gl_capture.tsv lists them) and dm/gfx/tools/gl_shaders.py translates them offline; the host finds each by the hash of its text

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# handheld: the Switch build plays by touch there (SDL turns the touch screen into LÖVE touches and mouse presses: tap a card, drag it), which on the iPhone are the touches no
# gamepad control takes, on the Mac the mouse; docked it reads only the pads. Its window is then the 1280x720 handheld display
# touch: the virtual gamepad starts in its Tap layout, every touch to the game (the pads' corners would cover Run Info, Options and the deck); its layout button brings back 2D / 3D
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk. subsdk0 / subsdk1 are NVIDIA's OpenGL and Vulkan drivers, which program the GPU through NvRm: never loaded, the GL layer answers
# The NPDM declares no system resource, so the game has no virtual address memory: nninitStartup gives its malloc a heap of the pool − used memory, which it maps only as it touches
# it; main's 264 MB bss counts as used memory
# no NVN shaders: the NVN tables stay empty (gl_shaders.py writes the GL library and its table, not the profile)

column2: Balatro has no NVN shaders (its GLSL shaders go through the GL layer)
